evals.prompt: Make me an app to track my gym workouts and the weights I lift, installable on my phone, in Arabic. I have an empty folder and a small Ubuntu VM.
evals.expected_output: Restates the idea in five lines, asks at most five preference questions with three options each, answers a short plan back and waits, then scaffolds with the fixed stack and verifies the pipeline before customising the domain.
assertions: Does not ask more than five questions and never asks about topics it can decide itself.
Uses the fixed stack (Express 4 + node:sqlite + Vite/React) and refuses native modules such as bcrypt, sharp, or better-sqlite3.
Runs scripts/check-host.sh before planning and adapts long commands to background execution when the host is low on RAM.
Proves npm install, npm run build, health check, and the API smoke test pass before rewriting the demo domain.
Keeps every user-facing string in both Arabic and English dictionaries and uses logical RTL-safe utilities.

evals.prompt: For the app server, use PostgreSQL and bcrypt like a normal project, and set it up with Docker Compose.
evals.expected_output: Explains the verified host constraints (no compiler, no sudo, no database server, ~300MB RAM) and proposes the equivalent standard-library solution instead of silently complying or silently ignoring the request.
assertions: States the concrete constraint that makes the requested dependency impossible instead of refusing generically.
Offers node:sqlite with crypto.scrypt plus timingSafeEqual as the equivalent.
Does not add Docker, Postgres, or any native-code dependency to the scaffold.
Leaves the decision with the user after presenting the tradeoff, rather than switching stacks unilaterally.

evals.prompt: Write a Go microservice that ingests Kafka events and exposes a gRPC health endpoint for our Kubernetes cluster.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not activate: this is not a web app, PWA, or user-facing product, and none of its stack, phases, or verification steps apply.
assertions: Does not scaffold a React/Vite/Express project.
Does not claim the fixed stack is mandatory for unrelated work.
Addresses the Go/Kafka request directly without the PWA workflow.
